newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy approves bill for third mobile phone.
newsitem.headline: Italy approves bill for third mobile phone.

text.p: The Italian cabinet on Thursday approved a bill setting out tender details for Italy's third mobile phone operating licence, a government official said.
The bill will now have to be ratified by parliament.
The government wants to launch the tender this autumn, with the licence expected to be awarded by the end of 1996 or early 1997.
Companies from both Italy and other European Union members will be allowed to bid for the licence.
The two existing cellular phone operators in Italy are state controlled Telecom Italia Mobile and Omnitel-Pronto-Italia, controlled by struggling information and technology group Olivetti.

Mediaset, the recently floated television and advertising arm of Silvio Berlusconi's Fininvest SpA empire, has already said it will be a bidder in partnership with the British Telecommunications Plc and Italian state-owned bank BNL's Albacom joint venture.
Italian media said this week state electricity company Enel , was also considering bidding for the licence.
